findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file-read failure (missing file, permissions, I/O error)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error that the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain-typed error and use map_err to convert io::Error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric field value
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the entire metrics load instead of returning a typed parse error for the offending record
findings.fix: return a typed ParseError, use .map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid { field: 1 }), and propagate via ?

findings.problem: (...)parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates any value above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a legitimate metric value of 70000 becomes 4464, corrupting downstream calculations with no error signal
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>().map_err(...), or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use index access on an unsized split result; if a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields this panics
findings.failure_mode: a CSV line without a comma (e.g. a header or comment) triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of a typed error
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to get (_name, value_str) for the two-field grammar, or parts.get(0)/parts.get(1) with map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs stdout I/O inside the data-loading pipeline
findings.failure_mode: stdout is captured or redirected in production/CI, causing I/O errors that panic or corrupt output; metrics loading is no longer a pure calculation
findings.fix: move all println/logging to the shell layer; the core data-loading function must be side-effect-free

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line, even though only two fields are used
findings.failure_mode: unbounded per-line allocation amplifies memory pressure on large inputs; violates allocation discipline for bounded resource paths
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...)? to extract name and value directly without intermediate Vec; trim only the two needed substrings

findings.problem: load_metrics collects into a Vec with no try_reserve, no domain cap, and no bounded allocation
findings.failure_mode: a very large CSV file can allocate unbounded memory; allocation failure during collect yields an OOM panic rather than a typed Allocation error
findings.fix: validate a max_rows domain cap first; use Vec::new() followed by values.try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before the collect

findings.problem: Record has pub name: String — raw primitive string carries no domain invariants; any caller can construct an invalid name
findings.failure_mode: empty, whitespace-only, or control-character names silently enter the domain; violates parse-don't-validate principle
findings.fix: create a newtype Name(String) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and character set at the parse boundary

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, stdout I/O (println), and domain construction into one function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation; cannot swap I/O backends; violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell function that reads the file and delegates to (2) a pure parse_metrics(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that contains no I/O

findings.problem: No tests, benchmarks, or proof artifacts exist in the crate to verify behavior, performance claims, or correctness
findings.failure_mode: no evidence that the code is correct, fast, or even compiles; Holzman evidence gate cannot be satisfied
findings.fix: add unit tests for load_metrics with valid/invalid/malformed inputs; add benchmarks for throughput; add doc-tests or property tests for parse invariants

missing_evidence: no unit tests for load_metrics with valid CSV, malformed CSV, missing file, and boundary-value inputs
no benchmarks to measure throughput or allocation behavior of the metrics loading pipeline
no benchmark/profiler evidence for any performance claim
no second-ring evidence for any allocation or latency claim
residual_risk: The crate has multiple BLOCKER violations: two unwrap panic surfaces, a lossy as cast, unchecked indexing on split results, hidden stdout I/O in the data pipeline, unbounded intermediate Vec allocation per line, and no bounded allocation with try_reserve. The architecture fuses shell I/O, parsing, and domain construction violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation. No tests or benchmarks exist. This code must not be promoted. All unwrap() calls must become typed error returns, the as u16 cast must be replaced with checked conversion, indexing must use split_once or get with map_err, println must be removed from the core, and allocation must use Vec::new + try_reserve with a domain cap. Even after repair, tests and benchmarks are required before any Holzman promotion gate.
